meta.strategicSummary: Day 27 of Hormuz closure has crossed a qualitative threshold: direct US-Israeli kinetic strikes on Iran's Arak heavy water facility and two flagship steel plants represent a dramatic broadening of the conflict from a maritime chokepoint dispute into a full-spectrum military-economic campaign against Iranian strategic infrastructure. Credibility of Iran's closure posture is now near-maximum (0.97) — the regime has existential domestic political reasons to hold the strait closed and escalate asymmetrically. Escalation cost E surges to 9.5 as conflict scope expands beyond any plausible 'limited strike' narrative. Brent at $111.72 reflects market pricing of sustained disruption but likely underestimates tail risk if Iran retaliates against Gulf energy infrastructure. The Ps (US guarantee) erosion continues as Gulf partners face uncomfortable alignment with nuclear-site strikes. The dollar trap remains fully active: Iran's industrial destruction paradoxically accelerates its yuan-settlement trajectory as the dollar system is perceived as the weapon being wielded against it.
meta.mostSignificantEvent: US-Israel strike on Arak heavy water facility (headlines 0 and 2) — this is the most significant event because targeting a nuclear-adjacent site crosses an internationally recognized threshold, transforms the conflict from conventional military into potential WMD-escalation territory, maximally hardens Iranian closure commitment, and risks drawing in Russian and Chinese diplomatic-military responses in defense of their JCPOA stakeholder positions.
